newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council endorses Westendorp in Bosnia post.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council endorses Westendorp in Bosnia post.

text.p: The Security Council unanimously endorsed on Thursday the appointment of former Spanish Foreign Minister Carlos Westendorp to succeed Carl Bildt of Sweden as the international community's High Representative for Bosnia.
Westendorp, who has been Spain's U.N. ambassador since last July, will oversee the implementation of the civilian aspects of the Dayton peace accords which ended the war in Bosnia 18 months ago.
He was appointed on May 30 at a meeting in Sintra, Portugal, attended by the countries involved in the Bosnia peace process and will take up his new post on June 20.

The Security Council, in its resolution agreeing to Westendorp's appointment and expressing appreciation to Bildt, reaffirmed that the High Representative was "the final authority" in the region regarding interpretation of the Bosnia peace accord's provisions on civilian matters.

Westendorp, a native of Madrid, has a law degree and joined Spain's foreign service in 1964, working mainly in European affairs in Madrid and in Brussels. He served as foreign minister from December 1995 to May 1996.
Bildt, a former prime minister, is returning to Swedish politics.
He recently warned in a speech in Sarajevo that Bosnia's fragile peace could collapse if the 31,000-strong NATO peacekeeping force withdraw in June 1998, as currently scheduled.
